title: Right torsors under continuous-function sheaves and their canonical maps
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a Hausdorff topological group $G$ with an open-subgroup identity basis which is compact or complete for its two-sided uniformity, use the continuous-function sheaf $F_G(U)=C(|U|,G)$ [def-sfb-continuous-set-presheaf], with pointwise multiplication. A right $F_G$-torsor is a set sheaf $P$ with natural right actions $P(U)\times F_G(U)\to P(U)$, satisfying $p1=p$ and $(pg)h=p(gh)$, such that $g\mapsto pg$ is bijective for every existing section $p$, and the sieve of objects admitting a section covers every object. Its isomorphisms are equivariant sheaf isomorphisms. For a field-valued point $x:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, its fibre here is the sections of the geometric inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] at the final object. Constant translations induce its right $G$-action. A section over $U$, and a lift $\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$, give a fibre element via the inverse-image unit. Restriction across a field embedding is the corresponding inverse-image unit followed by the canonical composition comparison. For $f:Y\to X$ and a continuous homomorphism $v:G\to H$, an along-map $P\to f_*Q$ is a sheaf map taking $pg$ to the image of $p$ times $v(g)$ restricted to $Y$; its fibre map is its adjoint followed by the inverse-image composition comparison. An extension presentation $P\times^{F_G}F_H=Q$ is a natural family of maps $q_U:P(U)\times F_H(U)\to Q(U)$, balanced by $q(pg,h)=q(p,v(g)h)$ and right equivariant, universal among balanced natural maps to arbitrary set sheaves. The induced map sends $p$ to $[p,1]$, also on fibres. For the classification, a normal torsor base packages a connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] quasi-compact scheme, normal in the sense that every stalk is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and a small profinite model of its finite-etale fibre-functor automorphism group [def-galois-fibre-functor]. A coefficient group packages a Hausdorff topological group with an open-subgroup identity basis and the disjunction: compact, or complete for the infimum of its left and right uniformities.
